title: Advance plan-session stages only through their exit gates

facts.note: The rule applies throughout any session started by the atdd plan command; session-wide guidance (free dialogue, operator-oriented stage naming, vocabulary separation) holds in every stage.
Only the advancement obligation is scoped to stage transitions; knowing the current stage and whether its exit state holds needs a session-state observer.
Whether dialogue concerns session stages versus WMBT job steps (steps.convention) is judged from the conversation.

fires: Any point in an atdd plan session, including free dialogue within a stage (stage naming and vocabulary separation still apply).
An atdd plan session is about to move from Intent to Attach, Attach to Compose, Compose to Ratify, or Ratify to authoring.
The planner is about to author plan artifacts before the operator has locked the decomposition.
The operator pivots mid-session and the planner considers returning to an earlier stage.
The planner names or describes session stages, or refers to WMBT job steps, during the session.
doesNotFire: Authoring or reviewing WMBT job steps under steps.convention outside any atdd plan session.
Work that is not part of an atdd plan decomposition session.

given: An atdd plan session runs the gated stages Intent -> Attach -> Compose -> Ratify, then author -> verify -> modify.
when: The planner is about to move the session to the next stage.
then: Advance only when the current stage's exit state holds: Intent = the main job is kept; Attach = sources and plan/ state are captured; Compose = the candidate decomposition is convention-shaped; Ratify = the operator has locked the decomposition.
prefer: Talk freely within a stage; the gate defines only the exit state, not a script.
Backtrack when useful: a pivot may reopen an earlier stage.
Name stages by what the operator is deciding, not by what the tool is doing.
avoid: Authoring anything before the Ratify gate; Ratify is the conversational->deterministic boundary (its rule is planner.plan.confirm-before-author).
Treating session stages and the WMBT job steps of steps.convention as one system or one vocabulary.
Advancing a stage when its exit state does not hold.
why: Gating on exit state keeps the decomposition dialogue flexible while guaranteeing nothing deterministic is authored until the operator has ratified a convention-shaped decomposition.
evidence: The session record shows, for each forward stage transition, that the exit state held: main job kept, sources and plan/ state captured, convention-shaped candidate decomposition, operator lock.
No authored plan artifact predates the operator's Ratify lock.
Reopening an earlier stage after a pivot is permitted and is not counted as a violation; it is optional, not required.
verifier_detail: Stage order: Intent -> Attach -> Compose -> Ratify, then author -> verify -> modify.

Term aliases: session_stages = the four gates with exit states; gate_not_script = dynamic conversation within a stage, gate defines only exit state, a pivot may reopen an earlier stage; ratify_before_author = Ratify is the conversational->deterministic boundary, nothing authored before it.
The Ratify stage's rule is named planner.plan.confirm-before-author (stage is Ratify, rule is confirm-before-author); do not expect a rule named after Ratify.
Session stage names are a separate vocabulary from WMBT job steps owned by steps.convention; do not match one against the other.
audit: Term ids in source: session_stages, gate_not_script, ratify_before_author.
Naming note: the Ratify gate's rule keeps the name planner.plan.confirm-before-author.

additions.text: Evidence items describing how session records demonstrate gate compliance.
additions.justification: Source states the gates but not how compliance is established; derived directly from the source exit conditions and backtracking permission without adding obligations.
Required by schema; derived from the source's session-wide statements, stage definitions and steps.convention separation.
